what_this_is: The Workshop row that keeps one held value under a name in the person's own vault, or removes the value held under a name, through the engine's held-values:put and held-values:remove door operations. The value comes on stdin, never on the command line.

payload.label: Keep a held value by name in my vault
payload.job: Keep one secret value (a key, a token) under a name in my own Trillion vault, or remove the value held under a name, so my tools and AIs can use it by name without ever seeing it
payload.description: Stores the value on stdin under the given name in the person's own vault through the engine's held-values:put operation, with the person's own key as the credential. The name is one the vault accepts, and a service connection's own names are refused by the engine. The value never goes on a command line, into a log or into the answer: the answer is {name, accepted}. Accepted means written at the writer, or queued sealed for the writer when this computer is not the writer. Connections keep their values through service-connections; use this for any other secret. With --remove NAME --issuer-status revoked|unknown it removes the value held under that name through held-values:remove instead, reads no stdin and answers {name, removed, issuer_status} (removed false when none was held) or {name, queued: true, issuer_status} when this computer is not the writer. Removing a held value does not revoke it at its issuer, so the caller says whether it was revoked there or is unknown.

items.description: The held value's name, one word; or --remove, the name, --issuer-status, then revoked or unknown.

invoke.stdin: the value, exactly as it is to be kept (one trailing newline is removed); none with --remove
needs: the person's own Trillion sign-in (trillion login, or the Mac app's key)
invoke.say: This runs on the person's own computer from the root of the Workshop checkout. Pipe the value in on stdin; never pass it as an argument. Report only the name and accepted.

provenance.source: New: the person's own door operation held-values:put (src/secrets.rs HELD_VALUES_PUT), replacing the store-file write of `secrets put`.
